analysis.investment_thesis: CAMS is genuinely one of the finest businesses I have seen in India — a toll-road on the nation's mutual fund industry with ROE of 44%, ROCE of 54%, and near-zero capital needs. I would love to own it, but at 40x earnings and P/B of 15x, I am being asked to pay full price for an already-recognized gem.
key_strengths: Near-monopoly economics: CAMS handles ~68% of India's mutual fund AUM as registrar — switching costs are enormous since fund houses cannot easily migrate crores of investor records
Exceptional capital efficiency: generates INR 359 Cr FCF in FY25 on total assets of just INR 1,726 Cr — a business that essentially mints cash without needing capital
Structural tailwind: India's MF AUM has grown from ~INR 10 lakh Cr to over INR 65 lakh Cr in a decade, and CAMS earns proportionally — the secular story is intact
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of 11.6% is moderate — CAMS earns a fee on AUM, so market corrections hit revenue sharply without proportional cost reduction
Zero promoter holding (0.00%) is unusual and creates governance uncertainty; 44.44% FII ownership means any global risk-off event triggers outsized selling pressure
SEBI regulatory risk — any cut in AMC-to-RTA fee arrangements or mandatory fee compression would directly impair earnings
red_flags: P/E of 40x and P/B of 15x price in many years of perfection — any growth disappointment will punish the stock severely
No promoter stake is a flag I watch carefully — management has no 'owner mentality' alignment beyond ESOP schemes
EV/EBITDA of 28.8x leaves essentially no margin of safety at current prices
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CAMS is the kind of business Charlie Munger would call 'inevitable' — the infrastructure layer beneath India's fastest-growing financial product category. The economics are extraordinary: 39% operating margin, 54% ROCE, and FCF that grows proportionally with AUM without meaningful incremental capital. The revenue step-up from INR 700 Cr (FY20) to INR 1,422 Cr (FY25) is driven entirely by India's investment culture expanding, not by management heroics. This is a wonderful business.

However, my fundamental rule is never to overpay, and at 40x trailing earnings, the market already knows how good CAMS is. The price-to-sales of 12.6x implies the stock is priced like a global SaaS company, not a B2B financial infrastructure business. I would need the price to correct to roughly 25-28x earnings — implying a 30-35% decline from here — before I would act aggressively. Until then, I admire from a distance.
